title: Read the following three primary source excerpts and answer the prompt below.

documents.label: A
documents.citation: Tennessee Butler Act, Chapter 27, House Bill 185, enacted March 21, 1925 (Tennessee Acts, 64th General Assembly, public domain)
documents.excerpt: An Act prohibiting the teaching of the Evolution Theory in all the Universities, Normals and all other public schools of Tennessee, which are supported in whole or in part by the public school funds of the State, and to provide penalties for the violations thereof. Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Tennessee, That it shall be unlawful for any teacher in any of the Universities, Normals and all other public schools of the State which are supported in whole or in part by the public school funds of the State, to teach any theory that denies the story of the Divine Creation of man as taught in the Bible, and to teach instead that man has descended or ascended from a lower order of animals.

documents.label: B
documents.citation: Scopes Trial transcript, cross-examination of William Jennings Bryan by Clarence Darrow, Rhea County Circuit Court, Dayton, Tennessee, July 20, 1925 (public domain, Library of Congress)
documents.excerpt:
DARROW: Do you think the earth was made in six days?
BRYAN: Not six days of twenty-four hours.
DARROW: Doesn't it say so?
BRYAN: No, sir…I do not think about things I don't think about.
DARROW: Do you think about things you do think about?
BRYAN: Well, sometimes.
[Laughter from the crowd.]

documents.label: C
documents.citation: H.L. Mencken, "Homo Neanderthalensis," Baltimore Sun, July 29, 1925 (pre-1928 publication, public domain)
documents.excerpt: Such is the great capital of the Fundamentalists, such is the Athens of the Coca-Cola belt. What could be more lovely?…The yokels have been galvanized. They leap and cavort. They roll and cry. They are led by a prophet who knows all the answers. Bryan is their Moses and their Woodrow Wilson.
